Maya (Support): Thanks for the report, @Priya. We see the UI spinner + repeated 429s in the screenshot. Can you grab a HAR and the console log from your browser and attach them here? Please also copy a failing request as a curl so we can repro.

Priya (Customer): Yep, I can do that. Which browser should I use? I have Chrome on macOS and Edge on Windows.

Sam (Support): Either is fine. Quick steps for Chrome/Edge:
1) Open DevTools (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+I) -> Network tab
2) Check "Preserve log" and also enable "Disable cache"
3) Reproduce the issue
4) Right-click any request -> "Save all as HAR with content"
5) Console tab -> right-click -> "Save as..." to get console logs
6) For a single failing request: right-click -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL (bash)" and paste the result here (masking API keys)

Nina (SRE): A few extra asks for us:
- Include the response headers for the failing request (we look for `x-request-id`, `x-edge-id`, and status codes)
- If you see 401/429/502 responses, screenshot the headers pane
- Please redact your `Authorization:` header value and any cookies, but keep header names intact

Priya (Customer): Got it. I'll capture from Chrome on macOS. Should I zip everything?

Maya (Support): Yes, please zip the HAR + console log + screenshots. Upload to the support ticket and paste the ticket link here. Also paste the `curl` line in a code block. Example snippet we want:

```
curl 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: abc123def' \
  --data-raw '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Sam (Support): If the "Copy as cURL" contains `--compressed` or `--compressed --insecure` that's fine. We just need the request verb, url, and headers. If you can't share body, we can still repro from headers + timing.

devops-bot: [deployment] prod-2026-03-12-15:42 rolled out to us-east-1 :rocket:

Priya (Customer): Uploading now — attaching `repro_bundle.zip` to ticket #5421. Included HAR, console.txt, screenshot.png. cURL pasted in ticket. Let me know if you need more.

Nina (SRE): Received. I'll start by checking `x-request-id` across the logs and search the edge logs for that id. If we need a packet-level trace we'll ask for the exact time + timezone. Thanks!
